lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Standardize hyphens, en dashes, date formats, commas, capitalization, and separators throughout the résumé.
Order the Mobility Systems bullets so the most target-relevant work leads.
items.because: For ML engineering roles, model quality, production deployment, evaluation infrastructure, and efficiency should be prioritized.

items.says: Do not place the generic AI-first bullet before the two stronger technical Agent Runtime bullets.
Check PDF text extraction so bullets do not merge or break incorrectly.
items.because: Applicant-tracking systems rely on correctly extracted text.

items.says: Make the code URL clickable and ensure it leads directly to strong, current work.
Use the actual GitHub domain if the code URL primarily points to GitHub.
items.because: The current path looks generic.

items.says: Verify that PDF text extraction preserves the URL correctly.
items.because: Applicant-tracking systems need to read it correctly.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are irrelevant to technical qualifications, create privacy and bias concerns, and use valuable space.

items.says: Use an en dash rather than a hyphen in the date range.
items.because: Date punctuation should be consistent throughout the document.

items.says: Format “Expected” so it cannot be mistaken for part of the degree title.
Consider adding the GPA if it is strong.
items.because: A strong GPA may help the candidacy.

items.says: Replace the generic country and location placeholders in the actual résumé.
Use the same date style and separators as the graduate degree entry.
Use the institution’s official English name rather than an unofficial translation.
items.because: This matters if the institution is not well known in the target country.

items.says: Confirm that the October 2024–May 2025 dates are accurate and clearly show a completed role.
Consider identifying the internship as part-time if needed.
items.because: That may resolve a timeline question about its overlap with graduate school.

items.says: Clarify whether the 35% gain is relative or a percentage-point increase.
Identify the baseline for the 35% accuracy improvement.
items.because: The metric should be auditable.

items.says: State the evaluation set or case count behind the accuracy result.
items.because: The metric should be auditable.

items.says: Define “diagnostic accuracy” more precisely.
items.because: Readers need enough detail to judge the result.

items.says: Clarify what made the tool-use trajectories “validated.”
Keep the assistant-only masking detail only if it materially caused the outcome.
items.because: Otherwise it is too implementation-specific for the lead bullet.

items.says: Explain how reviewer disagreement was measured and over how many cases.
Show whether lower disagreement corresponded to greater adjudicated correctness.
items.because: Agreement alone is not necessarily a quality improvement.

items.says: Clarify whether “in-scope signals” means permissions, context filtering, routing, or feature access.
items.because: The current phrase is ambiguous to a technical reader.

items.says: Add “by” before both percentage reductions.
items.because: The current wording is grammatically incomplete.

items.says: Change “penalises” to U.S. spelling when targeting U.S. employers.
items.because: The résumé mixes U.S. context with British spelling.

items.says: State the scale of the GRPO evaluation.
Define how redundant tool calls were identified.
Clarify which SFT baseline was used.
items.because: It may be the adapter referenced elsewhere.

items.says: Consider simplifying “grouped tool-use rollouts.”
items.because: The phrase may add jargon without meaningful distinction.

items.says: Clarify how citation quality was scored.
State how many evaluation cases the harness used.
Distinguish regressions detected during development from regressions actually prevented from reaching production.
Clarify the harness’s usage frequency or integration into releases.
items.because: That would strengthen the adoption evidence.

items.says: Use a serial comma consistently in the metric list.
Delete this bullet because it duplicates the first Mobility Systems bullet without a separate outcome.
The claim that assistant-only loss masking makes the model reproduce tool outputs more faithfully is technically inaccurate.
items.because: Assistant-only masking generally prevents loss from being applied to non-assistant tokens rather than directly teaching tool-output reproduction.

items.says: Clarify the causal link between the triage branch and the 68% backlog reduction.
items.because: The résumé does not establish that the branch caused the reduction.

items.says: Provide the backlog baseline or approximate case volume.
Explain whether “800+ sensor signals” means per-case signals, available features, or raw channels.
Clarify whether the branch was launched in production, as a pilot, or in an internal workflow.
Confirm that the job title matches the official title used in background checks.
Replace “by 4x” with an unambiguous reduction expression.
items.because: It can be interpreted inconsistently.

items.says: Provide the before-and-after GPU memory figures.
Clarify whether throughput, training time, convergence, or model quality changed.
Specify the model family or training pipeline affected.
items.because: “The perception models” is too broad.

items.says: Verify that the work used BF16 mixed precision rather than merely converting stored weights.
State the request volume, concurrency, or production traffic conditions used in testing.
Confirm that caching and batching did not compromise data freshness or correctness.
Make explicit whether the load test runs in CI.
Fix the tense mismatch between “Maintained” and “adds.”
items.because: The verbs are inconsistent.

items.says: Clarify whether release cycles were shortened to three days or by three days.
items.because: The current wording says “to.”

items.says: Add the previous release-cycle duration.
Use a stronger verb than “Maintained” if the pipeline was materially changed.
items.because: “Maintained” may undersell the actual ownership.

items.says: Identify what the regression checks covered.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether they tested model quality, performance, packaging, compatibility, or deployment.

items.says: Clarify whether the 30 items were independently scheduled services or jobs within fewer services.
items.because: Technical readers may question the architecture.

items.says: Add a measurable reliability or operational result if available.
Ensure “dead-letter” is not split across lines in the PDF or extracted text.
Replace “Owner” with a role designation that states whether you created, maintain, or lead the project.
items.because: “Owner” is vague.

items.says: Add a repository or project link if the work is public.

items.because: The current bullet lacks both.

items.says: Add a user count, baseline, adoption measure, or measurable result.
items.because: The claims about delivery and outcomes are not verifiable.

items.says: Use present tense for this ongoing project.
